lacuna.name: unattended-loop-supervision
lacuna.repo_anchor: The supervised object is the local loop of the weco fork: weco-cli 0.4.0, resolved sha 0111f27e per .host-software ('uv tool install from the fork directly, weco 0.4.0'). Source at /tmp/weco-cli-bug/weco/local/loop.py: (a) run_eval executes subprocess.run(['bash', '-c', eval_command], ...) with NO timeout parameter (line 36) - a hung eval blocks the whole campaign indefinitely; (b) make_opencode_step raises RuntimeError('the opencode harness exited {code}') on any nonzero opencode exit (lines 111-112) - one harness crash aborts the entire multi-day run; (c) the loop is 'for step in range(steps)' with no resume - restart loses everything; (d) the post-mortem surface already exists: append-only .weco/local-loop/steps.jsonl per step with {step, value, improved_best, output_tail (last 2000 chars)} plus a final report.json (lines 74-85), which is exactly the heartbeat file an external watchdog can monitor. MEMORY.md 2026-09-08 records the host already invented this doctrine once for the turing_lab probe driver: 'the probe driver gained abort-on-consecutive-failure and model/outdir args', and NEXT-WINDOW-RUNBOOK.md carries the open/probe/verdict/committed-run/weco/close sequence the supervisor would wrap; local lanes are logged 'via weco observe (local JSONL)'. GPU windows are ~10h, making a single hang a whole-window loss.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09 the ecosystem is layered, and each layer has a mature incumbent. (1) OS supervision: systemd is the standard - Type=notify/exec with Restart=on-failure (not always) + RestartSec + StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst to stop restart storms; hardware watchdog via WatchdogSec with sd_notify WATCHDOG=1 pings at half the interval from a dedicated thread (freedesktop.org systemd.service and sd_notify docs; Red Hat 'self-healing services'); sd_watchdog_enabled() lets the same script degrade gracefully outside systemd. systemd-run transient units (--unit=, --property=Restart=on-failure, --remain-after-exit) supervise one-off overnight jobs with no unit file and give journalctl -u for the morning review (freedesktop systemd-run docs; systemd 257 supports unprivileged transient units). (2) Terminal layer: tmux survives SSH disconnects only (not reboots); remain-on-exit on + respawn-pane -k for manual restart, with the caveat that newer tmux may respawn a plain shell instead of the original command (tmux/tmux#1928); tmux-resurrect/continuum for reboots. 2026 adds agent-specific layers: tmux-assistant-resurrect (saves assistant session IDs/flags/env and relaunches after crash, Feb 2026) and amux, a purpose-built AI-terminal supervisor with configurable no-output stall detection that nudges or restarts the session, crash restart with the original prompt/context, auto /compaction near context limits, and per-session token/cost dashboards (stall-timeout default not published [uncertain: amux-stall-threshold-default]). (3) Cluster/CI: k8s liveness probes exist precisely to catch 'running but unable to make progress' deadlocks, with startupProbe gating liveness for slow starts (kubernetes.io); Colin Breck's essays document how misdesigned liveness reduces availability. GitHub Actions has timeout-minutes per job/step (default 360m, docs/community#14834), NO native retry keyword - operators use step-level retry actions, 'gh run rerun --failed', or workflow_run watcher workflows; fail-fast: false and max-parallel for matrices; re-run does not re-run dependent jobs (actions/runner#2810). SLURM: --requeue plus Node Health Check run via HealthCheckProgram at fixed wall-clock intervals, sacct/seff for post-hoc (slurm.schedmd.com FAQ; Crusoe/TensorWave docs). (4) Process-level timeout: GNU coreutils timeout (the 'timeout wrapper' class - note: coreutils, not glibc, despite the brief's phrasing): --signal=TERM --kill-after=grace with exit-code contract 124=timed out, 137=SIGKILLed; escalation exists because processes can trap/ignore TERM (GNU coreutils docs; SO 687948; unix.SE 21542). (5) ML-training-specific: MosaicML Watchdog (retry_on_system_failure, max_retries default 10) restarts a run from the BEGINNING on system/node failure; checkpoint autoresume (Composer autoresume + save_interval) is a deliberately separate mechanism (docs.mosaicml.com). PyTorch's NCCL watchdog is a heartbeat monitor - 'Watchdog caught collective operation. Heartbeat monitor timed out!' - with 600s default considered too long, ~40s recommended (NVIDIA/NeMo#9563); the classic GPU hang signature is logs stop while GPU utilization spikes to 100% (PyTorch forums); Coreweave documents that healthy-looking GPU utilization can hide stalled training (stragglers); the consensus stall signal is a PROGRESS heartbeat (completed steps / touched file mtime), never process or GPU liveness (OneSourceCloud). (6) LLM-agent overnight loops: Karpathy's autoresearch (2026, 630-line script) runs ~100 experiments overnight on one GPU by giving every experiment a fixed 5-minute wall-clock budget and waking to 'a log of experiments' - timeboxing per step, not watchdoging, is its supervision; TrainerAgent (arXiv 2311.06622) packages training-as-a-service with a training agent. The canonical liveness-vs-progress contract is AWS Step Functions activity tasks: HeartbeatSeconds (worker liveness) must be < TimeoutSeconds (total task deadline), yielding distinct failure causes so a heartbeat loss means the worker died while an overall timeout means the task ran too long. Timeout theory: Dean & Barroso 'The Tail at Scale' (CACM 2013) hedges at P95; MIT PRIMES 2024 evaluates percentile-based adaptive timeouts; SLO-aware load-adaptive timeouts appear in IEEE Access 2025; gRPC guidance separates keepalive/idle (no bytes flowing = hang) from deadline (too slow). (7) Test-harness precedent: pytest-timeout 2.4.0 - signal method (SIGALRM, POSIX-only, fails when the hang sits in a C extension or subprocess wait; fixtures not torn down, pytest-dev/pytest-timeout#134) vs thread method (cross-platform, dumps all-thread stack traces, kills the whole session), commonly paired with pytest-forked for isolation. (8) Post-mortem tooling: Python stdlib faulthandler (PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1; dump_traceback_later(timeout) doubles as an in-process watchdog timer; register(SIGUSR1) for on-demand kill -USR1 dumps); py-spy dump --pid attaches zero-setup to an already-hung process and prints every thread's stack (--nonblocking in containers); journald/coredumpctl and SLURM accounting provide the after-action record.
lacuna.applicability: Transfers directly to weco-local: (1) Eval timeout with escalation - wrap run_eval in coreutils-timeout semantics: subprocess timeout, then SIGTERM the process GROUP (start_new_session=True + os.killpg, because bash -c spawns children a bare pid-kill orphans), wait a grace period, then SIGKILL; exit contract 124/137 kept distinct from harness failure. This is the single highest-value change: today one hung eval blocks the 72h campaign forever. (2) Two-tier time budget, the Step Functions split: per-step deadline (adaptive = rolling P95 of observed step durations times a multiplier, floored and capped; fixed default for the first steps) + a hard campaign deadline; a slow step may extend once and be logged, a step with no progress signal is killed - that is HeartbeatSeconds vs TimeoutSeconds applied to a step loop. (3) Progress heartbeat, not liveness: the fork ALREADY writes append-only steps.jsonl per step; an external watchdog polling its mtime/growth detects a hung eval or hung harness even when the process is alive and the GPU busy (the Coreweave/PyTorch false-liveness signature). Wrap the whole campaign in 'systemd-run --user --unit=weco-<campaign> --property=Restart=on-failure --property=RestartSec=60 --remain-after-exit' so a crashed harness restarts and journald becomes the morning-review substrate. (4) Bounded-retry harness policy: replace 'raise RuntimeError' on opencode nonzero exit with retry-N-with-backoff, then skip-step-and-continue (best-so-far survives), aborting only on C consecutive failures - the probe driver's existing abort-on-consecutive-failure heuristic adopted verbatim. (5) Resume: steps.jsonl is already append-only; resume = re-read history on start, take last step index + best value, continue - avoiding MosaicML's documented failure where the watchdog restarts from the beginning because autoresume is a separate mechanism. (6) Post-mortem enrichment: per-step wall duration, exit code, status (ok/timeout/killed/skipped), retry count in steps.jsonl; on watchdog fire, py-spy dump (or faulthandler SIGUSR1) the hung child BEFORE killing, so the morning review has the hang's stack; extend report.json with per-status counts and a failure summary. Does NOT transfer: k8s probes (no cluster - the host is two GPUs driven directly); GitHub Actions machinery (only doctrine transfers: per-lane timeout, fail-fast:false equivalents, rerun-failed-jobs discipline for the morning); SLURM NHC/--requeue (no scheduler); MosaicML's cloud watchdog (restart-from-beginning semantics is the anti-pattern here); amux itself (Claude-Code-oriented product, closed supervision surface - only its stall/nudge/restart ladder and auto-compaction ideas transfer).

design.mechanism: Concrete contract, implementable cold. (A) Eval execution with escalation: proc = subprocess.Popen(['bash','-c',eval_command], cwd=workdir, start_new_session=True, stdout=PIPE, stderr=STDOUT, text=True); try: out,_ = proc.communicate(timeout=budget); except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGTERM); try: out,_ = proc.communicate(timeout=kill_grace); except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGKILL); out,_ = proc.communicate(). budget = clamp(4 x rolling_P95(prior step durations), floor=300s, ceiling=hard_cap); fixed default until 3 steps of history exist. Step status recorded: ok | timeout | killed | skipped. (B) Harness-failure policy: on opencode nonzero exit retry up to R=2 times with 30s x attempt backoff; on final failure append a {status: skipped} step entry and CONTINUE (never abort the campaign); abort only on C=3 consecutive failed steps (the probe driver's existing heuristic). (C) External supervisor: systemd-run --user --unit=weco-<campaign> --property=Restart=on-failure --property=RestartSec=60 --remain-after-exit wrapping 'weco local ...'; a sidecar watchdog shell loop checks 'find steps.jsonl -mmin +<stale_min>' (stale_min ~ 3x median step duration); on stall it first py-spy dumps every child pid (stacks land in journald), then kills the step process group via the pidfile the loop supervisor exposes, letting the in-loop timeout policy or systemd restart take over. (D) Resume: on start, if steps.jsonl exists, parse the last entry; next step = last index + 1, best_value = max/min over history; never rewrite prior entries. (E) Post-mortem schema: extend each steps.jsonl entry with {started: iso8601, duration_s: float, status: ok|timeout|killed|skipped, exit: int, retries: int} keeping the existing value/improved_best/output_tail; report.json gains counts per status, the timeout/skipped step list, best-so-far with its step index, and the captured watchdog stacks. Exit-code convention preserved end-to-end: 124 = eval timed out, 137 = eval SIGKILLed after grace, nonzero-opencode = harness failure (retried), 0 = clean.
design.failure_modes: Documented in the wild: (1) Watchdog kills slow-but-progressing work - GPU/CPU liveness heuristics false-positive on stragglers (Coreweave) and liveness misdesign causes restart loops that reduce availability (Colin Breck); defense: progress heartbeat (steps.jsonl growth) as the only stall signal, adaptive budgets from measured history, not utilization. (2) Signal-based timeout never fires when the hang is inside a C extension or a subprocess wait - SIGALRM is simply not delivered (pytest-timeout#134, pytest-timeout docs); defense: kill from OUTSIDE via the process group with TERM-grace-KILL escalation; never trust in-thread alarms for the eval child. (3) Restart storms - Restart=on-failure without StartLimitBurst/RestartSec loops forever and can wedge a GPU box; defense: rate limits, bounded retries (R=2), consecutive-failure abort (C=3). (4) Watchdog restarts from the beginning and loses the campaign - MosaicML's watchdog explicitly does not resume from checkpoint; defense: append-only steps.jsonl + resume-on-start. (5) Auto-restart masks root cause - McCanna's GPU watchdog is alert-only by design because a human distinguishes stuck from legitimate in seconds and power/NCCL root causes get buried by auto-restart; defense: capture stacks (py-spy/faulthandler) BEFORE the kill, alert-first on first occurrence of a stall signature, auto-kill only after capture succeeds or times out. (6) tmux as supervisor fails two ways: respawn-pane starts a plain shell instead of the original command (tmux#1928) and sessions do not survive reboot; defense: tmux is an attach surface only, systemd-run is the supervisor. (7) Retry poisons measurement - a killed eval returning a stale/partial metric line would corrupt best-so-far; defense: on timeout/killed status force value=None (no-improve), the loop already treats None as non-improving, plus the existing fresh-subprocess-per-step isolation keeps the next eval clean.
design.effort_estimate: Mostly wrapper-level with one small fork-level patch. Fork-level (weco-cli, precedent: bug PR connollydavid/weco-cli#1): run_eval timeout + process-group escalation (~20 lines), loop retry/skip/continue + resume-from-steps.jsonl (~40 lines), steps.jsonl schema extension (~10 lines). Wrapper-level (tools/campaign-runner, new): systemd-run invocation + stale-mtime watchdog sidecar + py-spy capture + morning summary generation (~100 lines shell/python, no new dependencies). Doctrine-only: morning-review checklist appended to the window runbook.
design.priority_signal: For: the current loop fails in exactly the three ways supervision exists to fix - the only blocking subprocess has NO timeout (one hung eval parks the 72h campaign forever), any harness crash aborts everything (raise RuntimeError), and any restart loses all progress (no resume) - on a host whose MEMORY records entire 10h GPU windows lost to a silent half-done revert and a broken lane, so the blast radius of one hang is a full window. The materials are stdlib-only (subprocess timeout, killpg, append-only JSONL) and every pattern has a decade-old production incumbent (systemd, Step Functions, coreutils timeout, pytest-timeout). Against: the campaigns actually run so far are ~10h windows with a human at open/close - 72h unattended is the stated goal, not yet the practice - so an alert-first watchdog (McCanna's position) may be the right first rung before auto-restart machinery, which brings its own failure modes (restart storms, masked root causes, MosaicML-style progress loss); and the resume half of this item overlaps the checkpoint-resume-iterative-loops and multi-lane-coordination items, so the supervision proper should land as: timeout+escalation, bounded retry, heartbeat watchdog, post-mortem capture - with resume semantics coordinated in that sibling item.
